messages.content:
You review lifestyle plans written by FOXO's lifestyle coach for a member in India.

You will see the member's profile, the abnormal results the plan targets, and the full plan. Judge whether a member could act on the plan tomorrow. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- specific: Recommendations give concrete foods with portions or timing, not generic advice like "eat healthy".
- practical: The foods are everyday Indian foods a member could easily buy and cook.
- explained: Each recommendation says how it helps the linked biomarker.
- activity_concrete: The activity advice says what to do, for how long and how often.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Diet: jain. Allergies: none. Conditions: none.
Abnormal results: triglycerides 210.0 mg/dL (high), vitamin_d 18.0 ng/mL (low)

Plan:
Focus areas: Lower high triglycerides with a high-fibre, low-refined-carb Jain diet; Address low vitamin D with fortified foods and safe sun exposure; ask your FOXO doctor about supplements; Build sustainable activity and sleep habits
Foods to eat:
- At lunch and dinner, start with 1 katori (about 150 ml) of moong or masoor dal soup or dal, and replace refined-flour rotis with 1–2 bajra/jowar/ragi rotis. (why: Dal and millet fibre help lower triglycerides by replacing refined carbohydrates and improving satiety.; linked to triglycerides)
- Use whole millets for 2 meals daily: 1 cup cooked foxtail millet khichdi/upma or 1–2 millet rotis per meal; keep total cooked grain to about 1 cup per meal. (why: Whole millets have more fibre than refined grains and help reduce triglyceride-rich very-low-density lipoprotein production.; linked to triglycerides)
- Fill half the plate at lunch and dinner with 1–2 katoris of seasonal non-root vegetables such as lauki, tinda, parwal, bhindi, beans, spinach or methi, cooked with 1 tsp oil. (why: Non-starchy vegetables add fibre and volume with few calories, supporting triglyceride control and weight management.; linked to triglycerides)
- Include one Jain-friendly protein at each meal: 1 katori dal, 1 katori curd, 30–40 g paneer, or 1 katori sprouted moong/moth beans. (why: Protein and fibre at meals improve fullness and reduce intake of refined carbohydrates that raise triglycerides.; linked to triglycerides)
- For snacks, eat 1 small handful (about 20 g) of unsalted almonds/walnuts/pumpkin seeds or 1 tbsp flaxseed powder; choose unsweetened, honey-free versions. (why: Unsaturated fats and flax fibre can support lipid improvement when used in place of fried or sweet snacks.; linked to triglycerides)
- If you take dairy, have 1 cup fortified milk or 1 katori fortified curd daily with a meal; check the label for vitamin D fortification. (why: Fortified dairy is a practical food source of vitamin D in a Jain vegetarian diet; ask your FOXO doctor whether a supplement is needed.; linked to vitamin_d)
Foods to limit or avoid: Sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets, mithai, sweetened drinks, fruit juices, and sugar-coated cereals; Deep-fried snacks such as samosa, pakora, puri and bhajji; keep these rare; Refined-flour foods such as maida bread, naan, bhatura, cakes, biscuits and white pasta; Large amounts of ghee, butter, cream and coconut oil; use small measured amounts; Sweetened curd, lassi, milkshakes and packaged beverages; For Jain diet: avoid onion, garlic, honey and root vegetables such as potato, carrot, beetroot, radish and ginger
Activity: No exercise restrictions were noted by your doctor. Aim for 20–30 minutes of brisk walking 5 days a week, plus 15–20 minutes of safe morning sunlight on arms/face 3–4 times a week. If any discomfort occurs, stop and follow your doctor’s advice.
Sleep: 7–8 hours per night; keep regular sleep and wake times and avoid screens for 30 minutes before bed.
Retest in 12 weeks

Nothing is generic like 'eat healthy'.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "practical", "reasoning": "All foods are everyday Indian staples (moong/masoor dal, bajra/jowar/ragi rotis, lauki, tinda, bhindi, curd, paneer, sprouted moong, almonds) available in any Indian market, and the plan correctly respects Jain restrictions by excluding onion, garlic, honey, and root vegetables.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "explained", "reasoning": "Each food recommendation carries an explicit 'why' statement linking it to the relevant biomarker, e.g., millet fibre reducing VLDL production for triglycerides and fortified dairy as a vitamin D source. The sun exposure link to vitamin D is stated in the focus areas, though the activity line itself does not restate it.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "activity_concrete", "reasoning": "The activity advice specifies what to do (brisk walking, morning sunlight on arms/face), duration (20-30 minutes walking, 15-20 minutes sunlight), and frequency (5 days a week, 3-4 times a week respectively), which a member can follow tomorrow.", "passed": true}]}
